punchline: A surgeon's hardest hours in the operating room can also be their most satisfying ones.
thirty_sec: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi found that surgeons often experience flow during operations. Surgery has everything flow requires: a challenge that matches skill, clear goals and instant feedback. In flow, a scattered mind becomes ordered, and self-consciousness disappears, yet the self emerges stronger afterwards. His broader point: work, not just leisure, can be one of the richest sources of flow.
question: Which part of your work absorbs you so completely that time disappears?
